issues.description: CHANGELOG entry and PR/title/check directory mismatch ('multiple_network_interfaces' vs 'single_network_interface').
issues.detail: The PR description and title say 'compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces', but the new directory, metadata CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG entry all use 'compute_instance_single_network_interface'. Pick one canonical name and align PR description, docs, and the hub URL in metadata so downstream tooling and operators are not confused.

issues.description: GKE bypass via name prefix is trivially spoofable and undocumented in metadata.
issues.detail: Treating any instance whose name starts with 'gke-' as MANUAL lets an attacker silence a FAIL by naming a VM 'gke-evil'. GKE-managed nodes are better identified via labels (goog-gke-node) or metadata. At minimum, document the heuristic in metadata Notes and add a TODO; ideally check labels/metadata instead of the raw name.

issues.description: Zero-interface case silently returns PASS, masking a likely data-collection bug.
issues.detail: When interface_count is 0 the report keeps status='PASS' with a 'has no network interfaces' message. A real GCE instance always has at least one NIC, so 0 indicates a parsing/API failure or a stopped/odd resource — surfacing it as PASS hides the problem. Consider MANUAL or skipping the resource entirely.

issues.description: Test 'test_compute_no_instances' does not set compute_client.project_ids, unlike other tests.
issues.detail: Other tests set compute_client.project_ids = [GCP_PROJECT_ID]; the empty-instance test omits it. It happens to work because the loop is empty, but for consistency and to avoid future flakiness if execute() ever references project_ids, set it here too.

issues.description: Network appliance use case (ip_forward=True) not handled despite being called out in the description.
issues.detail: The metadata Notes and PR description mention that network virtual appliances legitimately need multiple NICs, but only GKE is special-cased. Instances with ip_forward=True (a strong appliance signal already on the Instance model) still FAIL. Consider treating ip_forward=True multi-NIC instances as MANUAL as well.

issues.description: compute_service_test asserts instances[1].network_interfaces is empty, but the fixture is not shown to omit networkInterfaces.
issues.detail: The new assertion 'len(...network_interfaces) == 0' on instance2 depends on the test fixture deliberately omitting networkInterfaces for that VM. Confirm the mocked API response truly returns no networkInterfaces for instance2; otherwise this assertion will fail when fixtures are regenerated. Worth a brief comment in the fixture for future maintainers.

review.summary: The check is well-tested and the service-layer addition is clean, but several issues should be addressed before merge. The biggest concern is the naming inconsistency between PR title/description ('multiple_network_interfaces') and the actual implementation/CheckID/CHANGELOG ('single_network_interface'). The GKE-detection heuristic relies on a spoofable name prefix and ignores the ip_forward signal that the description itself calls out for network appliances. The zero-interface branch returning PASS silently hides probable data-collection failures. Minor test consistency nits round out the review.
